Import RedCap paindrawEM JSON data

Source: R/pdr_import_json.R
pdr_import_json.Rd

Reads JSON files generated by the RedCap paindrawEM module and converts them into a pdr_tibble (see pdr_match() for the terminology).

Usage

pdr_import_json(files)

Arguments

files

Character vector (or list coercible to character) of file paths.

Value

A pdr_tibble (see pdr_match()) with one row per successfully file in files and columns pdr_data (a pdr_list of pdr_drawings) and id (copied from .id). Non-existing files give a warning and NA in pdr_data, with id derived from the file name; files with invalid JSON give an empty list() and NA in id; NA entries in files give NA in pdr_data and id. On invalid files input, an empty list().

Details

Each input file is expected to contain a single pain drawing. Multiple files can be provided and will be combined row-wise.

Supported JSON formats

The format is detected per file, so files of different formats can be mixed in one call:

  • Schema 1.0 (see schema/paindraw_schema_1.0.json): has a schema_version key (any 1.x). Fields: drawing_id, module_version, app, timestamp, width, height, units, template_file, template_md5 and strokes, where each stroke has stroke_id, draw_input_type, tool, color, line_width, spray_density, spray_radius, alpha, scale_factor, device_pixel_ratio and points ([x, y] pairs).

  • Old format (v0.3): no schema_version, but the keys v, id, w, h and s. Fields: id, v, w, h, units, tpl, app, ts and s (strokes, with strokeId, drawInputType, tool, lineWidth, color, alpha, sprayRadius, sprayDensity and the coordinate list-column p).

A file in neither format (or with an unsupported schema_version) gives a warning and an empty placeholder row, as for invalid JSON.

Transformation details

Both formats give the same result:

  • The metadata fields are renamed to the pdr_drawing elements .id (id / drawing_id), .version (v / module_version), .width, .height, .units, .timestamp, .app and .template_file (tpl / template_file); .file is set to the file path. Other fields are dropped. .template_file is NA if the file has no template name.

  • Coordinates are converted into the .points tibble with columns .index (the position of the stroke in the file), .x and .y.

  • The y-axis is flipped using the drawing height (.height) so that the origin is in the lower left corner.

  • The remaining stroke properties are stored in the .strokes tibble, with columns .index, .draw_input_type, .tool, .tool_width, .color, .alpha, .spray_radius and .point_density. Pen strokes in schema 1.0 have NA for the spray columns.

Failure handling

If files is not a character vector (or list coercible to one), or is empty, a warning is given and an empty list() is returned. A file that does not exist, or whose content is not valid JSON, gives a warning and is kept as a placeholder row, so that rows stay aligned with files: its pdr_data element is an empty list() and its id is NA_character_. Downstream functions drop such placeholder rows with a warning.

An NA entry in files is not a failure: its pdr_data element is NA and its id is NA_character_ (NA in, NA out).

A valid file without any strokes (s is empty) is not a failure: it gives a drawing whose .points and .strokes are zero-row tibbles with the usual columns.

Examples

# Load a single file
json_file <- pdr_example_file("1_palmar.json")
pdr_import_json(json_file)
#> # A tibble: 1 × 2
#>   pdr_data          id                          
#>   <list>            <chr>                       
#> 1 <named list [11]> PID4193-R1F-palmar-E13885-I1

# Load multiple files (here, the same file twice)
pdr_import_json(c(json_file, json_file))
#> # A tibble: 2 × 2
#>   pdr_data          id                          
#>   <list>            <chr>                       
#> 1 <named list [11]> PID4193-R1F-palmar-E13885-I1
#> 2 <named list [11]> PID4193-R1F-palmar-E13885-I1

# Plot imported data
pdr_import_json(json_file) |>
  pdr_plot_xy(background_image = pdr_example_file("bg_lower_arm_palmar.png"))
